deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages of cote 154): a fixed arrangement of pseudo-lines is drawn in orange. An extra pseudo-line D, drawn in green, sits in some 'position relative' with respect to it. D̃ appears to be the closed lift of D, a circle with an antipodal involution (the lift of a projective pseudo-line to the sphere). The orange lines cut D̃ into arcs.

A 'transition arc' a on D̃ is an arc along which D can be pushed across an orange crossing. There are two kinds, both grouped under transition arcs on the next page:
- An 'arc de spécialisation': D bounds a triangle with an orange vertex, and pushing ('balayage', sweeping) makes D pass through that vertex.
- An 'arc de généralisation': D already passes through a vertex and can be pushed off it ('antibalayage').
In the figures D bulges over the vertex after the move, and the transported arc is called b. Pol(D) seems to be the polygon structure on D̃ given by its cut points. There is a canonical isomorphism Pol(D) ≅ Pol(D') for a specialization.

The page defines a 'rotation' operation ρ on flags (D, ω, a), where ω is an orientation of D̃ and a a transition arc. ρ(D, ω, a) = (D', ω', a') where:
- (a) D' is obtained from D by performing the transition along a;
- (b) ω' is the opposite of the orientation transported from ω;
- (c) a' is the next transition arc on D̃' after the transported arc b, in direction ω'.

The NB records how sweeping and antisweeping act on the three local pictures. The cases are listed as I 1), I 2), II 1), II 3), i.e. two pairs. Group I is for a a specialization arc (D' bumps over the vertex). Group II is for a a generalization arc (D' dips under it). The page states 'deux' (crossed out) but four pictures are drawn.

Lemma: a' can be computed in either of two ways.
- Take the transition arc a'_0 following a on D̃ in the direction opposite to ω, and transport it by sweeping or antisweeping.
- Or transport a to b and take the ω'-successor of b.
Justification: under a specialization, Pol(D) ≅ Pol(D') gives a bijection between the transition arcs not adjacent to a and the transition arcs of D' other than the antipode of b (completed on p.104).

Purpose: ρ is a face-tracing permutation of a combinatorial map on the 'graph of positions' (vertices = positions D, edges = transitions). Composing a flip with orientation reversal and stepping to the next arc is exactly how faces of a ribbon graph are traced. The orbits of ρ are 2-cells; p.104 shows a 4-cycle (1)→(2)→(3)→(4)→(1). This builds a 2-dimensional cell complex of positions of a moving pseudo-line, presumably to compute its Euler characteristic or topology. Cf. the count 2ν−2+(ν+2)=2ν+2 on p.104, apparently a count of transition arcs (ν−2, 2, ν, 2).
errors: The case count: 'deux' is struck and the text says the cases group 'par deux paires', so four cases are meant, matching the four drawn pictures.
The justification is incomplete on this page. The stated bijection covers specialization; the generalization case is only implied by symmetry (antibalayage), and is continued on p.104.

The definition of a' relies on b not being an endpoint ambiguity. On p.104 G. himself flags possible exceptional specialization arcs ('blocage des couleurs') not yet checked, so the well-definedness of ρ is not fully verified.

ideas.what: Flip / transition of a pseudo-line across a vertex of an arrangement, split into specialization (onto a vertex) and generalization (off a vertex), called balayage/antibalayage
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flip (mutation) in pseudoline arrangements; sweeping; degenerate (non-simple) position as an intermediate stratum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for flip connectivity; Goodman–Pollack (1980s) for sweeping; Edelsbrunner–Guibas (1986) for topological sweep

ideas.what: Operation ρ on flags (position, orientation, transition arc): flip, then reverse orientation, then take the next transition arc
ideas.modern_name: Face-tracing permutation of a combinatorial map / rotation system, giving a 2-dimensional cell structure on the flip graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Edmonds, Tutte, Cori (combinatorial maps); 2-cells of flip complexes in Manin–Schechtman higher Bruhat orders (1989)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck uses cartes and their permutation description in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not for pseudo-line position complexes

ideas.what: Lemma: the successor arc can be computed either before or after the flip, via the canonical isomorphism Pol(D) ≅ Pol(D') restricted to non-adjacent arcs and arcs other than the antipode of b
ideas.modern_name: Local compatibility of flips with the cyclic order of cut points (local structure of the flip complex)

missed.claim: G. builds an explicit 2-complex (a combinatorial map) on the space of relative positions of a green pseudo-line with respect to a fixed arrangement, with faces given as orbits of ρ. He leaves open exceptional arcs related to 'blocage des couleurs'. This 'one moving line' complex, as opposed to the full flip complex of arrangements, seems not systematically studied as a map whose ρ-orbits are faces.
missed.quote: Opération de rotation autour d'un f[?] par une flèche de transition orientée (D, ω, a)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It relates to single-element extensions of oriented matroids (Las Vergnas, Bokowski–Sturmfels) and the topology of extension spaces. That is a known hard area: the extension space conjecture is false in general by Liu (2020), but well behaved in rank 3. A ribbon-graph description could give Euler-characteristic proofs of the rank-3 sphericity.

missed.claim: Grothendieck is applying the combinatorial-map (dessin) formalism, a flag permutation whose orbits are faces, to the flip graph of pseudoline arrangements in 1983–84, contemporaneous with the Esquisse.
missed.quote: ω' est l'orientation opposée à celle déduite de ω par transport
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical link between his dessins/cartes viewpoint and the combinatorics of pseudoline arrangements and oriented matroids, a link absent from the secondary literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is local and routine, but this is a careful unpublished construction of a face-tracing permutation on positions of a pseudo-line, linked to extension spaces and the Esquisse map formalism, and not recorded in the literature.
